newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil drifts sideways.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil drifts sideways.

text.p: Singapore gas oil drifted sideways in quiet trading late afternoon on Tuesday as the market slowly adjusted back to business after the long Lunar New Year and Eid-el-Fitri holidays, brokers said.
"The market is still very quiet and people are only now getting warmed up," one broker said.
The March gas oil swaps were last quoted at $25.50/$25.65 per barrel from Thursday's $25.90/$26.05 with one lot traded earlier at $25.65, brokers said.
Lower prices were partly due to the weaker overnight gas oil closing on London's International Petroleum Exchange, where March ended down $4.00 per tonne at $181.25.
Traders said the market may edge up later today as there are expectations of new buying interest from regional consumers as well as Singapore-based players.
On the physical market a 200,000-barrel cargo traded late Thursday at $25.30 per barrel free-on-board Singapore, higher than the two deals seen on Wednesday at $25.20 and $24.90 per barrel.
Jet fuel prices are steady at a high level with the March jet fuel/gas oil spread last quoted unchanged at $2.55/$2.90 per barrel, brokers said.
Fuel oil swaps were quoted weaker in thin trading with March seen at $101.00/$102.50 per tonne, down from Thursday's $102.25/$103.00, brokers said.
